## Review: What is wrong with this representation?
<hr>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:250px; LEFT:20px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:350px" SRC="images/march.jpg">

- **The “March of Progress” is one of the most iconic — and most misleading — images in science communication.**

<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 60%;">

- **Reality: Evolution is not a straight line; it's a branching tree**

<br/>

- **Reality: Evolution has no goal or direction**
    + evolution is not creating modern humans as an 'end goal'

<br/>

- **Reality: There were many species of hominins with varied adaptations**

<br/>

- **It reinforces misleading (racists/ablesit) hierarchies from primitive to advanced humans**

</div>

## The complexity of being human
<hr>
<br/>

- **In addition to other harmful fallacies this cartoon propagates, it makes “being human” seem very simple, very separate, and very independent**
    + As we evaluate the role of humans in global change, are any of these things true?

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:280px; LEFT:150px; WIDTH:800px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/humanevolv3.png">

## Human Independence Revisited
<hr>
<br/>

***Homo sapiens* wouldn’t exist without our complex evolutionary, ecological, and societal associations**

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:260px; LEFT:50px; WIDTH:1000px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/notalone.png">

## Is independence just another human fallacy?
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 45%;">

- **This isn’t only “external” but also internal**

<br/>

- **<span style="color:blue">Example 1: your microbiome</span>**
    + >10,000 species occupy human body
    + 80-100 genera

<br/>

- **39 trillion microbial cells including bacteria, viruses and fungi live on-in us**
    + 'cell-wise' the human body is 43% human
    
<br/>

- **Human microbiome has 500x more genes than human**
    
</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:500px; WIDTH:600px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/microbiome.png">

## What does it mean to be *Homo sapiens*?
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:50px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/virus.jpg">

<div style="float: right; width: 55%;">

- **<span style="color:blue">Example 2: (barely) hidden in your DNA</span>**

<br/>

- **~8% of human genome is viral DNA**

<br/>

- **~40% human genome is repetitive DNA which also likely has a viral origin**

<br/>

- **100,000 pieces of ancient viral DNA live among our genes**
    + function, if any, has long been unclear
    
</div>
    
## What does it mean to be *Homo sapiens*?
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:50px; WIDTH:325px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/neand.png">

<div style="float: right; width: 65%;">

- **<span style="color:blue">Example 2: (barely) hidden in your DNA</span>**

<br/>

- **Most humans have 2% Neanderthal DNA**
    + remember - both species co-existed and sometimes mated 

<br/>

- **Neanderthal allele variants range in diverse expression of skin and hair color to immune function and neuropsychiatric disease**
    + may have left us prone to allergies!
    + may have caused some to have higher risks from Covid!
    + possible genetic links to depression and addiction

</div>

## What does it mean to be *Homo sapiens*?
<hr>


<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:275px; LEFT:20px; WIDTH:325px; HEIGHT:350px" SRC="images/denis.jpg">

<div style="float: right; width: 65%;">

- **<span style="color:blue">Example 2: (barely) hidden in your DNA</span>**

<br/>

- **Denisovans left genetic traces in oceanic and Asian regions**
    + genomes of Australian aborigines, New Guineans and Pacific Islanders ~5% Denisovan
    + East and South Asians up to .5%

<br/>

- **Denisovan allele variants range in diverse expression of immunity, metabolism and neurology**
    + gene variants in Tibetans regulates hemoglobin levels and allowing survival at high altitudes
    + alleles may allow better pathogen recognition and defense in Asian populations
    + variant in zinc transporter gene associated with predisposition to depression
 
 </div>
 
## Review: We are not 'independent' because we persisted
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:15px; WIDTH:600px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/denis2.png">

<div style="float: right; width: 43%;">

- **How separate or independent our we?**
    + perhaps.....just enough.....
    + 87 specific genes in modern humans are different from related genes in Neanderthals and Denisovans
    + <span style="color:blue">Potential clues for our survival?</span>

</div>


## Why did humans win the survival race?
<hr>
<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">
- **Was it key 'human' traits?**
    + many of these were shared (bi-pedalism, tools)

<br/>

- **Was it evolution of larger brains?**
    + Neanderthals were slightly larger!

<br/>

- **Was it fire?**
    + H.erectus may have used fire before we evolved

<br/>

- **Was is related to social aspects**
    + survival of the friendliest

<br/>

- **Was it related to our adaptability**?
    + climate was unpredictable
    
<br/>

- **Was it something non-human?**
    + superior microbiome

 </div>
 
<div style="float: right; width: 45%;">
 
- **Was it luck?**
    + were we 'independent' enough?
 </div>   
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:250px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:430px" SRC="images/race.jpg">

## Human migration and megafauna impact
<hr>

- **Human expansion linked to extinction of large mammals**
    + During migration, >150 megafauna went extinct
    + sheep to mammoth sized
    + America's and Australia most notable

<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 45%;">

- **Evidence in Eastern USA suggests hunting of megafauna**
    + clovis points (stone tools) found alongside megafauna remains
    + direct evidence in Appalachia is lacking

<br/>

- **Climate change combined with overhunting may have accelerated extinctions**

 </div> 
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/clovis.png">

##

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:50px; LEFT:50px; WIDTH:1000px; HEIGHT:600px" SRC="images/mega.jpg">


## The agricultural revolution was a game changer..
<hr>

- **The end of the last Ice Age brought about warmer and more stable climates**
    + ~10,000 BCE
    + favorable conditions supported experimentation with plant cultivation

<br/>

- **Humans domesticated plants and animals**     
    + more predictable food supplies and the ability to store surplus
    + transition from nomadic hunting and gathering to settled farming communities.

<br/>

- **Impact: Laid the foundation for the rise of permanent civilizations**

## Why does this matter for global change?
<hr>
   
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:250px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:300px" SRC="images/now.png">

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

- **Over human history...**
    + **Biomass of terrestrial vegetation has halved**
        + <span style="color:red">443 trees per human</span>
    + **More than 20% reduction in biodiversity**
        + <span style="color:red">terrestrial and aquatic</span>
    + **At least one million species threatened with extinction**
        + <span style="color:red">new discussions of an emerging mass extinction event</span>
    + **More than 70% of the Earths land surface has been altered by humans**
        + <span style="color:red">only 5% is left as 'pristine'</span>
    + **Total global biomass of wild animals today is < 25% of what it was during the Late Pleistocene**
    + **Terrestrial vertebrates biomass today is represented by livestock (59%) and living human beings (36%)**.
</div>
